rv.q: “The Laugh Track” thus scores on all counts — writing, directing, acting, production design (with lighting by Donna Ruzika, sound by Hunter Moody and props by Patty Briles) and period costuming by Kim DeShazo.

Brown's excellent portrayal is that of a witty and ambitious woman, and through her portrayal, it is clear that she is a determined to be successful in a career that doesn't have much female representation.
The sitcomish approach playwright Wendy MacLeod has taken in The Laugh Track ends up less successful in execution than it might promise to be on paper.
Perfect scenes, perfect costumes, all the actors were on the dot with their characters.

I enjoyed The Laugh Track which, despite its title, elicited genuine laughs – and not canned laughter – from the opening night audience during this fast moving, scene shifting 90-minute mixture of comedy and drama.

cn.t: Critics mostly praise "The Laugh Track" for its sharp writing and behind-the-scenes look at I Love Lucy's creation, though one dissenter finds MacLeod's sitcom-style approach falls short of its promise.
